notes.title: The Qualities of a Protégé
notes.summary: Dr. Angel taught the 10 qualities of a protege, from being a master listener to honoring your mentor, with the ping pong coach illustration on strengthening strengths instead of fixing weaknesses. A bonus teaching covered liars, truth, and accuracy: how to tell deliberate deceivers from people who are simply inaccurate, and why accuracy has its place. The class also named guilt and shame as what keeps a protege from approaching a mentor, and pointed ahead to the next teaching, Discovering the Power of Purpose.
notes.full_text:
# NCU Class Notes — Thursday, October 29, 2026
Teacher: Dr. Angel. Topic: The Qualities of a Protégé.
(Summarized from the class transcript Ralph shared after class. Class ran past 7:26 p.m.; Ms. Lynn took attendance and closed in prayer.)

## The 10 qualities

1. **Be a master listener.** Total focus on the mentor: no calls, no texting, no reading. Part of listening is writing it down. A short pencil is better than a long memory. Never go before wisdom without pencil and paper.
2. **Learn and discern from an imperfect mentor.** No mentor is perfect in any of their roles. Extract good information from an imperfect source. You will not agree with every book in the program, and that is on purpose.
3. **Clearly define what success means to you.** Success is the fulfillment of a worthy goal. For the believer the heart of it is doing and fulfilling the will of God. Knowing your definition points you to your assignment and, in this context, to the right mentor: find a mentor who has developed success in the direction you want to go.
4. **The protégé pursues and chooses the mentor.** If the mentor chooses the protégé, that is control, not mentorship. The proof of your desire to grow is in your pursuit. The protégé decides how close he gets and how fast he grows. Do not let a mentor seeming out of reach put you off; they are human. A regular voice in your life carries a level of mentorship whether you planned it or not.
5. **Decide what you want to learn.** Set immediate goals: 90 day goals, one to two year goals, long term goals. Goals give focus, and people keep working at what they see growth in. And learn the 11th commandment: blessed are the flexible.
6. **Give your mentor feedback.** It helps the mentor recognize your filter: your thoughts, heart, and motivation. Tell them whether they are helping you or not.
7. **Never regret what you share with your mentor.** It is a personal relationship; unload wrong thoughts and let the mentor correct perspective. The mentor keeps what the protégé shares confidential, but the mentor's teaching may be passed on to others. You cannot move into your tomorrow with yesterday's information.
8. **Everyone has a weakness; a good mentor strengthens strengths.** A mentor concentrates on your strengths and develops them toward genius. A manipulator focuses on your weakness to keep you under. (Illustration: the Chinese ping pong coach, asked about weaknesses: "We ignore their weakness. Strengthen the strengths.")
9. **Be willing to invest in the relationship.** People are like elevators, they take you up or down; invest in the ones who take you up. Relationship costs time and expectation, and honor.
10. **Honor your mentor.** Honor their place in your life. It does not have to be money: sharing their words is honoring, showing up when they teach is honoring, influencing someone else with what they taught you is honoring. That is kingdom.

## Bonus teaching: liars, truth, and accuracy
- Everyone lies in the small sense (saying "I'm fine" when they are not); distinguish deliberate deceivers, who are few and not to be trusted, from people who are simply inaccurate or speaking from their perception.
- Never confront a liar. Take note of what they showed you and move forward; confronting just trains them to deceive better.
- Accuracy is a real gift and the world needs it, but it has its place: essential in a courtroom, less important over coffee with a friend. Not everyone inaccurate is a liar, and not everything accurate is the whole truth; perception shapes reports (50 people, same sunset, 50 descriptions).
- The Bible is the ultimate truth; a doctor's report can be honest and still not be the final word (testimony shared of a friend healed of kidney cancer after prayer and a 40 day fast).

## Also from class
- Guilt and shame will hinder a protégé from choosing and approaching a mentor; dropping them brings discernment.
- Next teaching coming: "Discovering the Power of Purpose," then goal setting. Classes run Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.
- NCU is reviewing and changing curriculum this year.
- Ms. Lynn closed in prayer, including prayer for help with reaction papers, dissertations, and theses.

## Follow-ups involving Ralph
- Dr. Angel asked Ralph about AI help: she is looking forward to seeing some AI canvas and marketing work, asked him to tell her what he wants and send it over, and said they still need to talk and will talk tomorrow (Fri Oct 30). She plans to combine it with other business.
- A classmate asked Ralph to email her the thing he posted on Facebook so she can use it in her dissertation; Ralph said "Feel free to." (Open: the email itself.)
- After class Ralph told the group what Muse did today: cleaned up and unpublished about 500 YouTube videos, scanned his Facebook posts, downloaded the songs, posted them to YouTube with written descriptions, and started the TikTok account the same way.

notes.title: Honor (Student Notes)
notes.summary: Fill in the blank student notes for the Honor teaching, in Minister Lynn's voice. It opens with 'Honor is the ____ of the Kingdom,' works through what the Bible says about honor (about 146 mentions in the KJV, roughly 355 with related words), five women and eight men God honored, the difference between honor and respect (Kavod, glory), and Dr. Murdock's wisdom keys on honor, including 'Everywhere you sow honor you reap favor.' Received from Ralph on November 19, 2026. The notes themselves carry no class date.
notes.full_text:
Honor Student Notes

Honor is the ____________________ of the Kingdom

We honor others not because they necessarily deserve it but because of who we are.

What does the Bible say about honor..?

If you do a word search in The Bible on the word "honor" you will see it is mentioned approximately 146 times in the KJV, however words relating to honor such as honorable etc would bring the total to roughly 355 times. The Biblical meaning of the word, "honor" is "profound respect, high esteem and the recognition of inherent value or worth." According to AI.

Throughout the Bible we see that God commands honor. The first time we see this is in the 10 Commandments and number 5. "Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee." (Exodus 20:12.)

We are also commanded to honor those older than us. "Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the Lord." (Leviticus 19:32.) and, "Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity." (1 Tim 5:1-2.)

I think we can agree that honor is a big thing to God. My Pastor Dr Murdock says, "Honor will get you further than genius." I agree. Honor has tangible rewards. If we look at the 5th Commandment the reward for obeying your parents (obeying is an act of honor) says that, "It will go well with you in the land." In (Proverbs 22:4) we see, "By humility and the fear of the Lord are riches, and honour, and life." Honor brings life.

5 women that God honored. Please look up the Scripture and write it next to each one.

1. Mary the Mother of Jesus
2. Mary Magdalene
3. The woman at Samaria
4. The woman with the issue of blood
5. The woman who adorned Jesus feet with perfume

What about men that God honored..?

- Abraham. God honored Abraham for his profound faith, choosing him to be the father of many nations and promising to bless the world through him.
- Noah. God honored Noah's righteousness and obedience by preserving him and his family through the great flood, saving them from the coming destruction.
- Moses. Despite his own feelings of inadequacy, God honored Moses by using him to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt, performing great miracles and establishing a covenant.
- David. Honored for his heart after God's own, David was a brave king and warrior, known for his strength and sincerity, though he also had his failures.
- Elijah. God honored the prophet Elijah by empowering him to perform mighty acts and by taking him to heaven in a chariot of fire.
- Elisha. As Elijah's successor, God honored Elisha with miracles and continued his prophetic work for Israel.
- Joseph. God honored Joseph for his faithfulness in a life of betrayal and hardship, which ultimately led him to a position of power in Egypt.
- Cornelius. A Gentile centurion, God honored Cornelius for his piety, prayer, and generosity, and used him to bring the Gospel to the Gentiles.

What is the difference between honor and respect..? Respect focuses on what someone has done, honor focuses on the position they carry. In Hebrew the word, "Honor" is Kavod which means glory. The word, "Honor" originates from the Latin word, "honos," the god of war.

Until we receive we have nothing to give so how do we receive honor from God..? (Hebrews 11:6) explains, "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."

Why is honor so important not only to God but to our very lives..? Honor and morals are very closely linked. Honor is our guide to living right. You might say that a person displays valor, honesty, empathy, compassion these are characteristics of honor. You can easily tell a person of honor, they do what is right behind closed doors when no one is watching, not just in public.

Who do you show honor to..? ____________________________________________________________

Who shows you honor..? __________________________________________________________________

Wisdom Keys of Dr Murdock on Honor

"Continual honor guarantees eventual access." Example I honored my Pastor Dr Murdock for years before he invited me to work for him which granted me access to him that others didn't have.

Who would you like access to..? __________________________________________________

"When you learn honor you have learned the secret to life." All promotion comes from honor.

"Everywhere you honor you will succeed. Everywhere you dishonor you will fail." Example - my gardener story.

"Who you honor reveals who you are."

"Honor creates access faster than genius"

My favorite one that I live my life by. "Everywhere you sow honor you reap favor. Everywhere there is favor there is Money."

"Honor does not reveal the value of another. Honor reveals YOUR value of another." I said earlier we honor because of who we are not who they are.

"Honor has a fragrance." What does that mean..? I personally am drawn to people who show me honor. You call me Ma'am or Minister Lynn or Lady Lynn you get my attention. You call me Miss or Lynn or sis you get less of my attention. (present company exempt.)

"Honor is earth's highest currency."

"Honor is not what a culture defines it to be. Honor is what God defines it to be." Example in the Chinese, Japanese and Korean cultures honor is when children of all ages from toddlers to adults will kneel and kiss the feet of their parents anywhere, anytime. They bow to their elders or bosses. Depending on the relationship and seniority depends on the depth of the bow.

"I know your Wisdom when I observe who you honor."

Do you honor someone's time by always being early or do you dishonor their time by always being late..?

Church - Jesus and The Holy Spirit arrive on time, what is your excuse for being late..?

The value you put on someone's time whether it be a face to face chat, a phone call or whatever tells me all I need to know about you.

Honoring your boss at work.

Do you honor your boss..? ________________________________________

How..? __________________________________________________________________________________________________

What if I told you that taking an extra "quick" 5 mins at lunch was dishonoring.

What if I told you that "borrowing" a pen or paperclip or photocopying your own personal documents on the work photocopier was dishonoring..?

What if I told you taking personal calls and/or scrolling your socials during work hours was dishonoring..? Break times excluded.

What if I told you that not carrying out your bosses instructions to the letter was dishonoring..? If I asked you to go buy me 5 boxes of cards. You went to the store and you saw they had an offer on, 6 for $10 and you see that 5 would cost $10.50 what would you buy me..? ________________________________________

Why..? ________________________________________

"True honor is never forgotten. Nor is dishonor."

What kind of experience do you want to be known for..? __________________________________________________________________

Do you live a life of honor..? ________________________________________

In what way..? __________________________________________________________________
